title: Single-call control: mechanisms and verdicts in one pass
description: A/B CONTROL ONLY. The original single-call design, retained to measure whether the two-call split changes any verdict. Emits fix_mechanisms and verdicts together, with the findings in context while the fixes are described - which is exactly the conditioning the split removes.

verdicts.description: Exactly one entry per reviewer finding supplied, in any order.

unmatched_fixes.description: Fixing commits no finding described. These are the recall misses and must be listed even when empty, so that a judge silently ignoring the fix side is detectable.

fix_mechanisms.description: Exactly one entry per fix supplied.

mechanism.description: What was wrong with the code, under what condition, with what consequence - not what the patch touched. An honest 'no identifiable defect repair' is preferred to an invented mechanism, since everything downstream compares against this as though it were real.

agreement.description: MECHANISM: the finding names the failure mode the fix addressed. LOCALITY_ONLY: same file or function, different mechanism - explicitly NOT a match, recorded separately so the correspondence-vs-mechanism gap is measurable. NONE: no relationship. TOO_VAGUE: the finding is not specific enough to be wrong, so it cannot earn a match.

fix_id.description: The fix this finding matches. Required when agreement is MECHANISM or LOCALITY_ONLY; omitted otherwise.

case_against.description: The strongest argument that this is NOT a match, stated before ruling. Required for every verdict including non-matches, where it is the strongest argument that it IS one. A judge that sees finding and fix together can rationalise agreement, so it must argue the other side first.

rationale.description: Why the ruling survives the case against it. Must name the specific failure mode, not the location.
